newsitem.title: USA: Treasury's Auten sees moderate U.S. growth.
newsitem.headline: Treasury's Auten sees moderate U.S. growth.

text.p: The U.S. economy is likely to continue growing at a moderate pace with inflation under control, a U.S. treasury official predicted Tuesday.

"The cyclical imbalances and inflationary distortions that might have been expected after nearly six years of economic expansion are notable by their absence," John Auten, director of the Office of Financial Analysis, told a meeting of the Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee of the Public Securities Association.

"At the present time," Auten said, "there are virtually no signs of demand inflation in product markets and only scattered indications of rising cost pressures, despite labor markets that are frequently characterized as tight."

Auten noted that growth in the fourth quarter showed a sharp acceleration to 4.7 percent from the third quarter's 2.1 percent pace, but he said there was nothing in the report of that statistic to suggest "safe speed limits" were being exceeded. He highlighted the chain-weighted price index, which came in at 1.8 percent, and said it indicated that inflationary pressures were subdued in the fourth quarter.

Looking at the inflation picture, the Treasury official said that the Labor Department's Employment Cost Index "appears to have bottomed out and it is drifting up a little, but still in terms of just a few decimal points."
He also said increases in total compensation have been held down by slow growth in benefit costs recently and said there is some question whether those costs will behave as favorably in the future.
However, he said that increases in total compensation costs can be, in part, offset by productivity gains.
Last Tuesday, the Labor Department reported that the Employment Cost Index rose 0.8 percent in the fourth quarter after a 0.6 percent increase in the third quarter.

Summarizing his view of both the gross domestic product and labor costs statistics released last week, Auten said, "On balance, there was little indication from last week's two key releases that either demand or cost pressures had intensified meaningfully by the end of the year."
